data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Bridges are physical objects governed by static laws; theories are logical constructs subject to conceptual refutation.","Engineering often uses probabilistic risk assessment, which Popper explicitly rejects for theory choice."],"overturn_conditions":["If engineering practice is shown to rely fundamentally on inductive probability calculations for safety certification.","If the analogy fails to capture the normative force of scientific preference."],"shared_structure":["Selection based on past stress tests rather than probability of future load.","Preference for the design that has failed least under extreme conditions.","Acknowledgment that past survival does not guarantee future integrity."],"source_memory_refs":["bridge_engineering_safety_margins"],"transfer_claims":["Just as engineers use the most tested bridge design without claiming it will never collapse, scientists use the most corroborated theory without claiming it is probably true."]},"claim":"Popper's preference for the better-corroborated theory is defensible on his own terms as a 'critical preference' grounded in the logic of testing rather than inductive probability;
